cities.d: the largest city in and capital of Guyana with fascinating wooden colonial buildings

hidden.d: Castelliani House, named after its architect. This building served as the residence of the prime minister in 1965-85, was rebuilt in 1993 and since it houses the national gallery, showcasing paintings and sculptures of Guyanese…
Offers exhibits on the past president and first lady of Guyana and the country's history.
Pontoon bridge built in 1978 that is the only connection between Georgetown and West Demerara.

A large free garden where families and people hangout. The Guyana zoo is located within the grounds of the gardens and south of the zoo there are Victoria Lilies - Guyana's national flower, they are huge lilies.
Memorial to the liberation of the slaves. The cultural centre forms a huge traditional Wai-Wai (native American tribe) hut.

x.intro: Georgetown is the largest city in and capital of Guyana. Georgetown is primarily the business and governmental seat of the country but its fascinating wooden colonial buildings also provide a different experience for tourists. Most tourists visit Georgetown as a launching point to the rainforests of the interior.

must.d: A very small zoo with DIY cages for the animals. A lot of the cages are too small for the animals they house. However, the zoo is a cheap way to spend an hour or two while in Georgetown.
Prominent Catholic church, built in 1920, with an altar bequeathed by Pope Pius XI.
One of the world's tallest wooden structures, this cathedral is as attractive inside as out. The church is built of tropical hardwood between 1892 and 1899, and the tower is 45 m high.
A museum with two floors showing the Amerindian heritage of Guyana. You can see artifacts, costumes, photos and archaeological founds.
Gothic Revival building dating from 1889 said to be "the most picturesque structure" in Georgetown.
Dating back to 1881, the interesting design of this iron structure and clock tower certainly make it the most recognisable of buildings.
It was built by the Dutch in 1817 and then rebuilt in 1830. This beacon has a colorful pattern of red and white stripes.

next.d: and is in the center of Guyana's rainforest. Its combination of great height and high water volume make it one of the most impressive waterfalls in the world.
where you can reach the border with Brazil. It is 14- to 18-hour journey primarily on a dirt road so be prepared.
Mini-buses leave at 04:00. Flights leave from Cheddi Jagan International airport later in the evening; from Ogle airport there at least two daily flights leaving, one early in the morning, the other…

x.safe: Georgetown is notorious for petty street crime. Do not walk alone at night, or even in the day, unless you know the area well. Areas such as the Tiger Bay area east of Main Street and the entire southeastern part of the city including, in particular, Albouystown and Ruimveldt are traditionally known as high crime areas but one can be relatively safe if going through these areas in groups and with native escorts.

hidden.d: Ruins consisting of small brick archway and some scattered foundations of a Dutch fort built in 1616 by Dutch captain Adrian Groenewegen that later served in repelling attacks by the British and French until the British finally…
Another aquatic resort, this one more geared toward playing in the tannin rich river or spring. While you're in the area, you can also take the Teperu Ferry across the wide Mazaruni River.

x.intro: Bartica is a river port town of some 8,000, known as Guyana's Gateway to the Interior, located just above the confluence of the Cuyuni and Mazaruni Rivers to the south. Its name comes from an indigenous word for "red earth."

x.intro: New Amsterdam is one of Guyana's largest towns on the eastern end of the Coastal Plain. It had a population of 17,329 in 2012.

x.around: Walk or drive. There's left-hand traffic in Guyana — watch out for cars that to you come from the "wrong direction".

hidden.d: Walk across the wooden bridge in Lethem to visit the community of St. Ignatius. There are no businesses other than a cashew factory cooperative run by local women.

Mount Roraima is at a height of 2810 m the tallest mountain in Guyana and marks the tri-border between Guyana, Brazil and Venezuela. It can reportedly be seen from Lethem, despite being over 200 km away as the crow flies.

n.en: English colonial-style houses all over the town

hidden.d: Gorgeous scenery. Those physically fit can explore the countryside. Confusing to get to on a map, but locals are happy to give directions.

cities.d: an extremely remote and undeveloped town surrounded by unspoiled rainforest

x.around: Walk, walk, walk. There are a couple of ATV's in the town, and they can be rented with a driver for short trips.
x.intro: Paramakatoi (sometimes spelled Paramakotoi) is a town in Potaro-siparuni in the Guyanese Highlands. This is an extremely remote area. Calling it a place to "get away" would be a great understatement — it is more like stepping back in time and witnessing subsistence living. Internet is reportedly available as of 2017. There are no restaurants and many people living here will have never seen an automobile.

intro: Guyana is an English-speaking country where you can find untouched South American nature, amazing wildlife and birding experiences, rich culture and heritage, and a multiethnic Caribbean vibe. 90% of the population live along the coast, leaving the country's interior untouched, and to be explored.

other.d: a genuine Amazonian experience for lovers of the jungle

x.around: Once you get out of the airstrip, it is easy to hike, explore and see the sights on foot.

hidden.d: A small village on the edge of the park.

x.intro: Kaieteur National Park is in the highlands of Guyana. The park offers a genuine Amazonian experience for lovers of the jungle.

must.d: The standout natural wonder of the park. The waterfall is the largest single drop fall on the planet. Though there are taller waterfalls, there is no other that matches its combination of height and water volume, making it…

x.safe: All of the usual precautions when exploring a tropical rainforest should be followed. You are encouraged to bring a hat, comfortable and cool clothing, shoes with good traction, an umbrella or raincoat just in case it rains, insect repellent (though there are carnivorous plants within the jungle that make your life easier) and if you are light-skinned, sunscreen.

other.d: a privately owned island retreat on the Essequibo River.

x.around: To get around you can either walk or hop on the minibus. Minibuses stop here to cross the river so you have a chance to negotiate the price. Be aware that most minubuses pass the river crossing in the morning and the evening. During the day transport is rare.
x.intro: Michelle's Island is a privately owned island on the Essequibo River, close to Kurupukari village and Iwokrama River Lodge in Guyana. It can be a retreat to break your trans-Guyana trip and relax for a couple of days.
